thread:
sofia: Quick sync — we just had a customer report: console rollout shows model_split=10/90 but an older feature-flag is returning 20/80. Users saw 20% new while console shows 10%.
raj: Oof. Current behavior is basically undefined: depends on eval order/last-writer. Bad UX. We need explicit precedence rules.
sofia: Agreed. Ops hit this hard. When they click the rollout button, that should guarantee routing unless a guard says otherwise.
marta: My preference: rollouts created in Console should win over ordinary flags, unless the flag is explicitly marked as "owned_by_app". But we need an automated way to surface that.
chris: Teams will be surprised if we flip semantics. Lots of services treat feature flags as their source of truth. We need compatibility and a migration path.
raj: Proposal: runtime evaluates guards, then evaluates rollouts and flags in parallel, returns an evaluation stack and an applied_origin field. Default precedence: guard(deny) > rollout > flag, but make precedence configurable at org-level.
sofia: Observability is critical. If we always return which rule applied, Console and telemetry can show exactly why a user saw a variant.
marta: Migration idea: add a controlled_by tag on flags (string, nullable). When Console rollout is created that overlaps a flag, backfill controlled_by=rollout:<id> and show a warning in Console/Flag UI. Provide a one-click transfer.
chris: Minimal API sketch to avoid large runtime changes. Return a transparent payload like:
```
{ "decision":"allow", "routing":[{"origin":"rollout","id":"r_42","weight":10},{"origin":"flag","id":"f_23","weight":20}], "applied_origin":"rollout", "applied_id":"r_42" }
```
That lets callers log exact source and lets Console display the applied decision.
raj: Runtime change is small: evaluate both sources but don't short-circuit yet. Compute applied_origin via precedence rules and return stack. No need to change core kernels.
sofia: UX: rollout detail page should list "overridden flags" with links and a one-click "transfer ownership" that sets controlled_by. Also show a padlock icon when rollout owns routing.
marta: Telemetry: add tag routing.origin (values: rollout|flag|guard) and emit routing.evaluation event with [request_id, applied_origin, stack]. Also a dashboard card for percent of requests where applied_origin != first_matched_origin.
chris: Edge case: guards that deny must be highest priority — deny wins even if a rollout would allow. So final evaluation order: 1) guards (deny/override stop), 2) rollouts+flags precedence, 3) default.
sofia: Ops wants a dry-run tool to preview binding: `rctl rollouts bind-flags --rollout r_42 --dry-run` that shows which flags would be marked controlled_by. We should also provide a migration job that backfills flags that overlapped >5% during past 30d.
raj: Performance: evaluating both sources per request adds lookup cost. We'll compute combined decision with a single pass and cache by key-prefix. KV caches and prefix caching should make per-request overhead negligible.
marta: Timeline: raj write API proto + spec by Tue. chris to draft rctl PR and runtime change by Fri. I'll mock UX flows next week. Sofia will coordinate comms to CS/Ops and propose an opt-in org flag during rollout.
chris: I'm +1 on rollout>flag default and guards highest. I'll add the telemetry events and dashboard queries.
raj: I'll author the API PR today. EOD Fri for the rctl follow-up.
sofia: Thanks. I'll open the RFC and link it here. px-deploy-bot: noted deployment.
px-deploy-bot: deploy complete: platform-api v2.14.0 -> staging :white_check_mark:
